studentResponse: {"rawAnswer":{"explanationQuestion":"Chemical reactions are fundamental to chemistry and understanding them helps us predict outcomes and ensure safety. I learned that reactions can be exothermic (releasing heat) or endothermic (absorbing heat), and this affects how we handle them. For example, exothermic reactions need cooling to prevent overheating, while endothermic reactions might need heating to proceed.","observationQuestion":"In the lab, I observed that when we mixed baking soda and vinegar, bubbles formed immediately and the temperature increased slightly. This showed me that chemical reactions can produce visible changes and heat. I also noticed that the reaction was faster when we used warm vinegar, demonstrating how temperature affects reaction rates."}}
